subproblem.title: Integrable densities on finitely many unit faces define a current: integrability (I) and existence (II)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. Let s be a finite set of pairs p = (ι, b), where ι : Fin n → Fin P is arbitrary (no monotonicity is assumed) and b : Fin P → ℤ. Let w : (pairs) → Euclid n → ℝ be such that w_p is Lebesgue integrable on Q₁ := {y ∈ Euclid n : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} for every p ∈ s. Write e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 ∈ Euclid P, Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (i ↦ (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} and E_p := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}). Then: (I) for every test n-form ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n (a C^∞ compactly supported n-form on Euclid P) and every p ∈ s, the function y ↦ w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p(y))(E_p) is integrable on Q₁; (II) there is a current D ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ n with D(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p(y))(E_p) dy for every test n-form ω.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (s : Finset ((Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ))) (w : (Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) → Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ), (∀ p ∈ s, IntegrableOn (w p) {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), ∀ p ∈ s, IntegrableOn (fun y => w p y * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ))) {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}) ∧ ∃ D : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), D ω = ∑ p ∈ s, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, w p y * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 5.1, displays (27)–(30) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1840–1885). The argument is steps 1–2 of the supplied proof of the selected node dimred_mbl_dtfr_face_integral_current, using its fact (F2) and the operator-norm half of its fact (F1). No monotonicity of ι is used.

Notation.
- n := m + 1 and e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ) ∈ Euclid P.
- Q₁ := {y ∈ Euclid n : ∀ i, 0 < y_i < 1}.
- For p = (ι, b): Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (i ↦ (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)} and E_p := (j ↦ e_{ι(j)}).
- For a test n-form ω: h_{p,ω}(y) := ω(Φ_p y)(E_p).
- ‖α‖ denotes the operator norm of a continuous alternating map α.

1. Φ_p is continuous. It is a constant plus the finite sum over j of the maps y ↦ y_j • e_{ι(j)}. Each coordinate y ↦ y_j is continuous (PiLp.continuous_apply), and constants, sums and scalar multiples of continuous maps are continuous (continuous_const.add, continuous_finsetSum, Continuous.smul).
2. h_{p,ω} is continuous. A test form ω is C^∞ (ω.property.1.1), hence continuous. Evaluation at the fixed tuple E_p is a continuous linear map on n-covectors (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ E_p). So h_{p,ω} = (evaluation at E_p) ∘ ω ∘ Φ_p is continuous. In particular it is a.e.-strongly measurable for volume restricted to Q₁.
3. Operator-norm bound. For every n-covector α and every p, |α(E_p)| ≤ ‖α‖ · Π_j ‖e_{ι(j)}‖ = ‖α‖, by ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm and ‖e_l‖ = |1| = 1 (PiLp.norm_single). This holds for arbitrary ι.
4. Test forms are bounded. ω is continuous with compact support (ω.property.1.2 : HasCompactSupport ω). So there is C ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ C for all x ∈ Euclid P (HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous). By step 3, |h_{p,ω}(y)| ≤ C for all y.
5. Proof of (I). Let p ∈ s. By hypothesis w_p is integrable on Q₁. By steps 2 and 4, h_{p,ω} is a.e.-strongly measurable and |h_{p,ω}| ≤ C everywhere. Hence y ↦ w_p(y)·h_{p,ω}(y) is integrable on Q₁ (Integrable.mul_bdd).
6. The linear functional. For ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n put L(ω) := Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} w_p(y)·h_{p,ω}(y) dy.
 - Additivity. The coercion of ω + η to a form is the pointwise sum, and evaluation of covectors is additive, so w_p h_{p,ω+η} = w_p h_{p,ω} + w_p h_{p,η} pointwise. Both summands are integrable on Q₁ by (I), so ∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω+η} = ∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω} + ∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,η} (integral_add, integral_congr_ae). Summing over p ∈ s gives L(ω + η) = L(ω) + L(η) (Finset.sum_add_distrib).
 - Homogeneity. h_{p,cω} = c·h_{p,ω}, so w_p h_{p,cω} = c·(w_p h_{p,ω}) and ∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,cω} = c·∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω} (integral_const_mul). Hence L(cω) = c·L(ω) (Finset.mul_sum).
 Thus L : TestFormOn univ n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ.
7. Uniform estimate. Let A := Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} |w_p|. Then A ≥ 0, since each integral of a nonnegative function is ≥ 0 (integral_nonneg).
 Claim: if δ ∈ ℝ and ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ δ for all x, then |L(ω)| ≤ A·δ.
 - For p ∈ s and every y, step 3 gives |w_p(y) h_{p,ω}(y)| = |w_p(y)|·|h_{p,ω}(y)| ≤ |w_p(y)|·δ.
 - The function y ↦ |w_p(y)|·δ is integrable on Q₁ (Integrable.abs, Integrable.mul_const). So |∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω}| ≤ ∫_{Q₁} |w_p|·δ = (∫_{Q₁} |w_p|)·δ (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, integral_mul_const).
 - Therefore |L(ω)| ≤ Σ_{p∈s} |∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω}| ≤ Σ_{p∈s} (∫_{Q₁} |w_p|)·δ = A·δ (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs, Finset.sum_le_sum, Finset.sum_mul).
8. Sequential continuity. Let (ω_j)_{j∈ℕ} be test forms with TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0. By definition there is a compact K ⊆ univ with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j. Also, for every k ∈ ℕ, iteratedFDeriv ℝ k ω_j → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k 0 uniformly on K, where 0 is the zero test form. Use k = 0.
 - Let ε > 0 and δ := ε/(A + 1) > 0. By Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff there is N with dist(iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0 x, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x) < δ for all j ≥ N and x ∈ K.
 - The coercion of the zero test form is the zero form, so its iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 at x is 0. Also dist(0, a) = ‖a‖ (dist_zero_left) and ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x‖ = ‖ω_j(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero). Hence ‖ω_j(x)‖ < δ for j ≥ N and x ∈ K.
 - If x ∉ K, then x ∉ tsupport ω_j, so ω_j(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and ‖ω_j(x)‖ = 0 ≤ δ.
 - So for every j ≥ N we have ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ δ for all x. Step 7 gives |L(ω_j) − 0| ≤ A·ε/(A + 1) < ε, because A ≥ 0 means A·ε < (A + 1)·ε.
 - By Metric.tendsto_atTop, L(ω_j) → 0.
9. Conclusion. The pair ⟨L, step 8⟩ is an element D of GeometricCurrentOn univ n: its two fields are exactly a linear functional on TestFormOn univ n and the sequential continuity at 0 proved in step 8. By construction, D(ω) = L(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p(y))(E_p) dy for every ω; this holds definitionally. Together with (I) from step 5, this proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: Φ_p is continuous and evaluation at the fixed tuple E_p is continuous linear, so h_{p,ω}(y) = ω(Φ_p y)(E_p) is continuous.
|α(E_p)| ≤ ‖α‖ (le_opNorm, ‖e_l‖ = 1), and a compactly supported continuous ω is bounded, so |h_{p,ω}| ≤ C.
(I): w_p·h_{p,ω} is integrable on Q₁ by Integrable.mul_bdd.
L(ω) := Σ_p ∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω} is linear by integral_add and integral_const_mul, using (I).
Order-0 uniform convergence on the common compact K, plus vanishing off K, gives sup_x ‖ω_j(x)‖ → 0, hence L(ω_j) → 0. Then D := ⟨L, continuity⟩ satisfies the formula by rfl.
